s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with cognitive impairment, dysarthria, and dysphagia
salient_findings: Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia over 6 months
Vertical gaze palsy and tongue atrophy
key_facts: Family history of memory problems after age 80
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene identified by whole-exon sequencing
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF

shortlist.label: TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene identified by whole-exon sequencing

shortlist.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Vertical gaze palsy and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Cognitive impairment, dysarthria, and dysphagia with family history of memory problems

shortlist.label: Corticobasal degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with cognitive impairment and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, along with symptoms such as progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs, supports this diagnosis. The severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging also aligns with frontotemporal dementia, particularly given the genetic finding.

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: While vertical gaze palsy is a hallmark of progressive supranuclear palsy, the genetic finding of a TBK1 pathogenic variant and the broader range of symptoms better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia. The specific genetic finding points more precisely to TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: Although tongue atrophy and pyramidal signs could suggest amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, the absence of clear evidence of widespread motor neuron involvement and the presence of cognitive impairment and vertical gaze palsy make this less likely.

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: This condition often presents with asymmetric parkinsonism and alien limb syndrome, which are not mentioned in the vignette. The genetic and imaging findings better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.
